column3: Close to the Hebrew; “put [it] on heart” is rendered “take it to heart,” and “honor” “glory.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the offspring” is rendered “your descendants,” and “dung” “refuse.”
Close to the Hebrew; “to be my covenant with Levi” is rendered “That My covenant with Levi may continue.”
Close to the Hebrew; “life and well-being” is rendered “life and peace,” and “I gave them to him, fear” “I gave them to him that he might fear Me.”
Close to the Hebrew; “instruction of truth” is rendered “The law of truth.”
Close to the Hebrew; “instruction” (torah) is rendered “the law.”
Close to the Hebrew; “by the instruction” is rendered “at the law.”
Close to the Hebrew; “lifting up faces in the instruction” is rendered “have shown partiality in the law.”
NKJV renders “the sanctuary (holiness) of Yahweh” as “The LORD’S holy institution.”
NKJV renders “one who wakes and one who answers” as “being awake and aware,” and moves “from the tents of Jacob” forward; the meaning of the phrase is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “from not still turning to the offering” is rendered “So He does not regard the offering anymore.”
NKJV renders this difficult verse as “But did He not make them one, Having a remnant of the Spirit? And why one? He seeks godly offspring”; the meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
NKJV renders “he hates sending away” as “He hates divorce,” and “he covers his garment with violence” as “it covers one’s garment with violence.”
